title: Forgotten Password
cardText: Recover access to Windows, Microsoft, email, website and business accounts.
Identify the account type and use the appropriate password recovery method.
Includes Windows local account recovery, bootable USB utilities and official account recovery links.
text: This guide covers forgotten passwords and Windows sign-in problems.
Identify the account type before attempting recovery.
Use supported account recovery methods first.
For local Windows accounts, specialist bootable recovery utilities may be useful when standard reset methods are unavailable.
Only perform password recovery on devices or accounts you own or are authorised to service.

identifyAccountType.title: Identify the account type
body: Determine whether the problem involves signing into Windows or another service.
Windows accounts may be local, Microsoft or organisation-managed.
Email, website and network accounts usually have separate recovery procedures.

windowsAccountType.title: Identify the Windows account
body: Check whether Windows uses a personal Microsoft account, a local account or an organisation-managed account.
A personal Microsoft account generally uses a Microsoft email address or another email registered with Microsoft.
A local account exists on the computer and does not require online Microsoft authentication.
Organisation-managed accounts should be recovered through the organisation's approved procedures.

checkWindowsAccountOptions.title: Check the Windows sign-in method
body: Determine whether the sign-in problem involves a Windows Hello PIN or the account password.
A Windows Hello PIN is different from the Microsoft account password.
Check whether Sign-in options provides another available authentication method.
If the computer is managed by a business or school, use the organisation's account recovery process.

checkPinOrManagedAccount.title: Identify PIN or organisation-managed account
body: Check whether the sign-in screen offers I forgot my PIN.
A personal Windows Hello PIN can often be reset using the associated account verification process.
If the account belongs to a business, school or domain, password recovery is normally controlled by the administrator.
Use the appropriate branch rather than attempting an offline local-account reset.

resetWindowsPin.title: Reset the Windows Hello PIN
body: At the Windows sign-in screen, select I forgot my PIN if available.
Complete the requested Microsoft account verification.
Create a new Windows Hello PIN.
If this option is unavailable, check Sign-in options for another supported authentication method.
A Windows Hello PIN reset does not necessarily change the underlying account password.

link.name: Microsoft: Change or reset a Windows PIN
link.description: Official Windows Hello PIN reset instructions.

recoverMicrosoftAccount.title: Recover the Microsoft account
body: Use Microsoft's official password reset process.
Complete identity verification using the account's registered recovery methods.
If the normal reset process is unavailable, use Microsoft's account recovery form.
After resetting the password, reconnect the Windows computer to the internet and sign in.
If the computer uses Windows Hello, the existing PIN may still provide access.
Bootable local-account reset tools do not reset the password stored by Microsoft's online account service.

checkLocalPasswordReset.title: Check supported local account recovery options
body: Check whether the Windows sign-in screen offers Reset password and previously configured security questions.
Check whether a password reset USB disk was created before the password was forgotten.
If another administrator account is accessible on the computer, it may be possible to reset the affected local account.
A password reset disk must have been created in advance.
If none of these methods is available, investigate specialist recovery options.

usePasswordResetOption.title: Reset the Windows local account password
body: Use the available Windows security questions, existing password reset disk or authorised administrator account.
Follow Microsoft's supported password reset procedure.
Create a new password and verify that the account can sign in.
Check access to the user's files and previously saved credentials after resetting the password.
Record the new password in a secure password manager.

link.name: Microsoft: Local account password reset
link.description: Official Windows local password reset instructions.

checkBitLocker.title: Check disk encryption before offline recovery
body: Before using a bootable password reset utility, determine whether the Windows system drive is protected by BitLocker or device encryption.
A locked BitLocker volume cannot be accessed by an offline recovery tool without the appropriate recovery key.
If encryption is enabled, locate the recovery key before attempting any changes.
Recovery keys may be stored in the owner's Microsoft account or the organisation's device management system.
Do not format, reset or modify encrypted storage simply to bypass the sign-in problem.
If encryption is not blocking access, offline local-account recovery may be considered.

link.name: Microsoft: Personal BitLocker recovery keys

bitLockerRecovery.title: Recover access to the encrypted drive
body: The Windows system drive is encrypted and cannot currently be unlocked.
Locate the matching BitLocker recovery key using its recovery key ID.
Check the owner's Microsoft account or contact the organisation managing the computer.
Microsoft cannot recreate a missing BitLocker recovery key.
Without the recovery key, the existing encrypted data may be inaccessible.
Avoid reinstalling or resetting Windows until important data recovery options have been considered.

link.name: Microsoft: BitLocker recovery key
link.description: Official information about locating and using BitLocker recovery keys.

offlinePasswordRecovery.title: Consider bootable Windows password recovery utilities
body: For an authorised local Windows account, a bootable recovery environment may be useful when normal reset options are unavailable.
Hiren's BootCD PE includes several Windows local-account password utilities.
Sergei Strelec WinPE is another maintenance environment containing recovery tools.
These utilities normally reset or remove a local Windows password rather than reveal the existing password.
They do not recover passwords for Microsoft, Google or other online services.
Check that the recovery tool supports the installed Windows version and storage configuration.
Offline password changes can affect access to encrypted files, stored credentials and other protected data.
Back up important data where possible before changing account information.
Only use these utilities on computers you own or are authorised to service.

localRecoveryComplete.title: Local Windows account access restored
body: The local account is accessible again.
Set a secure new password if the recovery method cleared the previous password.
Verify access to the user's files and applications.
Check whether previously saved credentials or encrypted files require additional recovery.
Consider configuring security questions, a password reset disk or another supported recovery method.
Store recovery information securely.

localAccountEscalation.title: Further Windows account recovery required
body: Standard and specialist local-account recovery methods have not restored access.
Check whether there is another authorised administrator account or an existing system backup.
Consider manufacturer-supported Windows recovery or account recreation if appropriate.
Preserve important user data before reinstalling or resetting Windows.
Check for BitLocker encryption and encrypted user files before making destructive changes.
If the computer belongs to an organisation, follow its IT recovery procedures.

link.name: Microsoft: Local account recovery options
link.description: Official password reset and Windows recovery guidance.

onlineAccountType.title: Identify the online account
body: Determine whether the password belongs to an email provider, website, cloud service or business network.
Personal accounts usually provide their own password recovery process.
Business and school accounts may require administrator-assisted recovery.
Windows local password reset tools do not recover passwords stored by online account providers.

useOnlineRecovery.title: Use the provider's account recovery service
body: Open the service's official sign-in page.
Select Forgot password or the equivalent recovery option.
Verify account ownership using registered recovery methods.
For Google or Gmail accounts, use Google's account recovery process.
For Microsoft email accounts, use Microsoft's account recovery service.
If the browser or password manager has an existing saved password, check it using the owner's authorised access.
Avoid unofficial recovery websites that request account passwords, verification codes or payment for guaranteed recovery.

checkRecoveryAccess.title: Check available account recovery methods
body: Determine whether the account owner can access the registered recovery email, phone number or authentication application.
Check for backup recovery codes, passkeys or an existing signed-in device where supported.
If an approved recovery method remains available, retry the provider's recovery process using that method.
If all recovery methods are unavailable, follow the provider's additional identity verification procedures.
A bootable Windows password utility cannot restore access to an online account.

retryRecovery.title: Retry recovery using an available method
body: Use an approved recovery email, phone number, backup code or existing authenticated device.
Complete the account provider's identity verification steps.
If the provider offers several recovery methods, select one that is accessible.
Once access is restored, update recovery information and create a secure new password.
If all available methods fail, use the provider's further recovery or support process.

providerEscalation.title: Further account recovery required
body: The normal online account recovery process was unsuccessful.
Use the provider's official recovery form or published support procedures where available.
Some providers have no alternative verification method when recovery information is unavailable.
Avoid services claiming they can recover any online account password.
Do not share verification codes or passwords with third-party recovery services.
If access cannot be restored, consider account replacement and recovery of any services linked to the lost account.

contactAdministrator.title: Recover a business or network account
body: Work, school, domain and network accounts are normally managed by an organisation.
For Microsoft 365 or Entra ID accounts, use the organisation's self-service password reset page if enabled.
For on-premises Active Directory, VPN, remote desktop or other managed accounts, contact the responsible administrator.
Verify account ownership and request an authorised password reset or account unlock.
Do not use offline local-account utilities to modify managed credentials without explicit authorisation.
If device encryption is involved, the organisation may also hold the recovery key.
